vulnerabilities.expectSeclayerFinding: unclear — no existing probe compares auth outcomes across locale-swapped sibling paths
vulnerabilities.actualResult: DETECTED (new capability) — "Language Route Auth Bypass (en gated, es is not)", CRITICAL, confidence:high, real evidence quoting the unlocked Spanish dashboard content.
vulnerabilities.notes: Initially MISSED: nothing in the scanner ever compared the SAME resource's auth outcome across two different paths — BOLA compares two IDENTITIES on one path, this needed comparing two PATHS for one (anonymous) caller. Built new server/i18nProbe.ts's probeI18nAuthBypass(): for every crawler-discovered path carrying an /en/ or /es/ segment, fetch it with no credentials; if that's gated (401/403), fetch the locale-swapped sibling ALSO with no credentials, and flag if the sibling returns 200. Deliberately symmetric (works whichever locale happens to be the buggy one, not hardcoded to 'en correct, es broken'). Read-only, two GETs, no state mutation — gated behind verified ownership like the other active probes since it's new requests, but otherwise as safe as the JWT/BOLA differentials it's modeled on. Re-verified detecting on the live scan.

vulnerabilities.endpoint: POST /api/es/auth/forgot-password issues a token redeemable via POST /api/en/auth/reset-password
vulnerabilities.actualResult: NOT DETECTED, confirmed — no probe exists for this class, by deliberate design.
vulnerabilities.notes: Manually verified working (a token issued under /api/es/auth/forgot-password is accepted by /api/en/auth/reset-password, and rejected by the locale-bound *-safe pair). Considered and rejected building a generic cross-locale-reset-redemption probe for two independent reasons, either alone sufficient: (1) PROVING it requires actually completing a password change — a real mutating action with a real consequence (the account's legitimate owner is locked out of their own current password) — the same non-destructive boundary established for Tier 2's price-manipulation/prototype-pollution/race-condition findings. (2) Even setting that aside, this is fundamentally unobservable to a real black-box scanner: in the real world the token is delivered by email, which the scanner has no access to; this fixture only makes the token visible by echoing it in the API response, purely for local testability (same convention as Tier 1's weak-session-token fixture), not because a real attacker could ever see it this way. Documented as an intentional scope boundary.

vulnerabilities.actualResult: DETECTED (new capability) — "Business-Logic Price Tampering (client-controlled price honored)", HIGH, confidence:high, RED_TEAM, real differential evidence. Same probe as T2-BizLogic-001.
vulnerabilities.notes: Closed by the same server/priceManipulationProbe.ts built for T2-BizLogic-001 (the two vulns are the same class). The probe sends two checkout requests differing only in unit price, with quantity>1, and proves the flaw when a response field equals price*quantity in BOTH — the server billed the client-supplied price. Non-destructive: no payment instrument and no confirmation are ever sent (so it can only elicit a quote/total, not a real charge), and keying on the computed price*quantity product excludes plain echo endpoints. The MXN/USD currency angle is the same underlying trust-the-client-price bug; the probe does not need to send a currency to prove it. Verified against the live fixture; does NOT fire on /api/checkout-safe.

vulnerabilities.actualResult: NOT DETECTED, confirmed — no probe exists for this class, by deliberate design.
vulnerabilities.notes: Manually verified working (10 rapid wrong-code attempts against /api/auth/verify-sms all return 400 with zero throttling; the *-safe pair correctly 429s after 3). Considered and rejected building a generic missing-rate-limit prober. The naive version — fire N wrong-code guesses and check none get throttled — looks safe in isolation (no money moves, no data changes, all guesses fail), but the actual risk is in the TESTING METHODOLOGY itself: against a REAL target that DOES implement a strict lockout policy (e.g. '3 wrong attempts locks the account for 24 hours', a common real design), the act of testing for the absence of a defense would itself TRIP that defense and lock out the legitimate account holder for real — a genuine, uninvited disruption the target owner didn't consent to for a routine scan. Same non-destructive-scanning category as the other three gaps in this tier, just via a different mechanism (risking a real lockout side effect, not a real financial one).

vulnerabilities.type: SQL Injection in Regional Business Logic (Estado Parameter)
vulnerabilities.actualResult: DETECTED — "SQL Injection (discovered parameter \"estado\" on /api/merchants)", CRITICAL, confidence:high, real evidence. Worked on the very first scan, no fix needed.
vulnerabilities.notes: Worth recording precisely WHY this worked without a fix, since a related raw-error format ("unrecognized token: '''", from the fuzzer's FIRST breaker, a bare single quote) is genuinely NOT matched by the current SQL_ERROR_SIGNATURE regex — confirmed by manual testing. Detection still succeeded because the fuzzer's THIRD breaker (') produces "near \")\": syntax error", which the Tier 3 Postgres-error fix's pattern already covers (it's the same 'near "X": syntax error' shape as the Tier 1 SQLite fix). Left the regex as-is rather than adding 'unrecognized token' speculatively — it didn't change this outcome, and only worth adding if a future real miss actually depends on the first breaker specifically.

vulnerabilities.type: Stripe Webhook Signature Bypass (Regional Currency Handling)
vulnerabilities.actualResult: DETECTED (new capability) — "Webhook Signature Verification Bypass (conditional on payload)", HIGH, confidence:high, RED_TEAM, real differential evidence (same invalid signature: rejected 400 for currency usd, accepted 200 for mxn).
vulnerabilities.notes: Re-examined after the user asked for a LESS-INVASIVE safe approach, and found one — built as server/webhookSignatureProbe.ts. The earlier objection ("proving it means the handler processes a forged payment") assumed a *payment.succeeded* event, whose acceptance credits an account = harm. But the signature skip here is gated on CURRENCY, independent of event type — so the probe instead sends a zero-amount charge.failed (a FAILURE event) for a NONEXISTENT entity: accepting that transfers no money and fulfills nothing (worst case a no-op/404), so proving the bypass causes no real financial side effect. The proof is a pure differential: the SAME invalidly-signed event is rejected under currency usd (signature verified) but accepted under mxn/eur/... (signature skipped) → conditional verification proven. Low-FP: requires the usd control to be REJECTED (so the endpoint really is signature-gating something) AND a non-usd currency ACCEPTED; an endpoint that verifies unconditionally rejects both (no finding), and one that accepts everything is left alone as ambiguous. Gated aggressive+owned; curated webhook-path list + discovered POST targets. Verified live against the fixture AND confirmed the probe only ever emitted charge.failed/amount-0 events (inspected the fixture PROCESSED log). Does NOT fire on /api/webhooks/stripe-safe (verifies unconditionally).
